title: Operator fallback experiment matrix and cost penalty catalog
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document captures a reproducible experiment matrix for operator-driven fallback strategies and an associated cost-penalty catalog used to evaluate trade-offs between SLO preservation and unit economics across regional surges. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and product engineers running controlled degradation experiments or designing automatic fallback policies.

Why this exists
---------------
- Fallbacks are a major lever for preserving SLOs during capacity scarcity or model regressions, but they have measurable cost and quality impacts.
- Operators need a concise experiment plan with metrics, dashboard queries, and a cost penalty model to compare candidate strategies.
- This doc standardizes experiment telemetry, rollout/rollback steps, and decision criteria for productionizing fallbacks.

Goals and scope
---------------
- Goal: Provide a repeatable experiment matrix that yields quantitative comparisons of: latency SLO retention, token-cost delta, quality regressions (evaluations), and operator intervention effort.
- Scope: Multiregion inference surface (hosted + dedicated), model variant fallbacks (quantized, smaller model families), and routing degradations (regional drain, tenant throttling).
- Out of scope: Model training/data pipelines, legal/customer contract negotiation.

Definitions and abbreviations
---------------------------
- Fallback variant: Any alternative response path (e.g., model C => model B, or cached response) used when the primary path is unavailable or overloaded.
- Cost penalty: Unit cost increase or revenue impact metric associated with using a fallback (e.g., tokens * $/token diff, or additional infra cost).
- SLO preservation: Fraction of requests meeting 95th percentile latency target and error-rate SLO.

Experiment matrix (canonical)
---------------------------
Columns: experiment_id | description | fallback_type | trigger | primary-metric | cost-metric | quality-metric | run-length | owner

Example rows (use these as templates):
1) EXP-001 | Model-variant degrade (Llama-70B -> Llama-13B-int8) | model_variant | queue-depth > 100 OR p95 latency > 600ms | p95 latency, error-rate | token-cost-delta-per-hour | eval-regression@20 prompts | 2h | operator-team
2) EXP-002 | Regional drain to peer region (eu-west -> us-east) | regional-routing | region capacity throttle 80% | p99 tail latency cross-region | egress-cost-delta | user-visible-quality (latency jump) | 4h | platform-network
3) EXP-003 | Prefetch cache fallback (serve from prefix cache) | cache_prefetch | cold-start rate > 30 req/min | mean latency | compute-cost-savings | correctness mismatch ratio | 3h | runtime-team
4) EXP-004 | Token-budgeted throttling for low-priority tenants | quota_throttle | burst credits exhausted | 95th latency of high-priority | revenue-at-risk | customer-error-annotations | 6h | platform-ops

Telemetry and dashboarding recipe
--------------------------------
Create a dedicated experimental dashboard with following panels per experiment run:
- SLO heatmap: p50/p95/p99 latency over time (per region, per tenant priority). Query examples:
  - latency_p95{experiment_id="EXP-001"} (PromQL)
  - request_duration_bucket_sum by (le, region)
- Cost delta stream: rolling token-cost-per-minute and infra-cost-surge.
  - token_cost_rate{fallback_variant!=""}
- Quality regression signal: evaluation pass-rate across a held promptset (20-50 prompts) run every 15 minutes.
  - eval_pass_rate{promptset="fallback-20"}
- Operator interventions: number and duration of manual rollbacks, with links to runbook tickets.
  - operator_rollbacks_total{experiment_id="EXP-001"}
- Composite KPI panel: cost-penalty vs. SLO-preservation scatter plot for each variant.

Minimum instrumentation checklist
--------------------------------
1) Annotate requests with experiment_id and fallback_variant in trace metadata.
2) Emit fallback_reason counter in request pipeline.
3) Record per-request token accounting and model_version label.
4) Attach prompt-set id for synthetic eval traffic.
5) Ensure operator actions log into the incident system with experiment_id tag.

Cost penalty catalog (examples and formulae)
-------------------------------------------
Catalog rows: fallback_variant | per-token-diff | expected-throughput | hourly-cost-delta | rollback-cost-estimate | notes
Example entries:
- L70B -> L13B-int8 | +0.002 $/token (lower cost) | 2k tokens/s | -$14.4 / hour per 1000 rps | negligible | reduced quality on long-form completion
- cross-region-eu->us | +$0.05 / 1k tokens (egress) | 1k tokens/s | +$180 / hour at 1000 rps | potential SLA credits | watch cold-start p95
- cached_prefix_response | -$0.001 $/token (savings) | N/A | -$3.6 / hour per 1000 rps | risk of stale content | requires invalidation policy
- quota-throttle-low | revenue-at-risk estimate (see calc) | depends on tenant mix | - | revenue-impact = average-MRR-per-req * blocked-reqs | requires customer comms plan

Cost calculations (short formulas)
- token_cost_delta_hourly = sum_over_requests(token_count * (cost_primary - cost_fallback)) per hour
- egress_delta_hourly = egress_bytes * egress_rate
- revenue_at_risk = blocked_requests * avg_revenue_per_request
Include these calculations in the dashboard as derived timeseries.

Experiment run playbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
1) Planning (2–4 days)
   a) Define hypotheses: e.g., "model-variant fallback preserves p95 latency with <5% quality regression and cost delta < $200/hr"
   b) Pick held promptset (20–50 prompts) and synthetic traffic profile matching customer mix.
   c) Create experiment_id, add telemetry tags and dashboard.
2) Preflight (1 day)
   a) Run synthetic traffic against fallback in staging and collect baseline metrics.
   b) Validate eval pass-rate and trace annotation.
   c) Pre-commit rollback playbook and test it in canary.
3) Execution (2–6 hours normally, up to 24 hours for long-run metrics)
   a) Apply experiment on a small cohort (1% of traffic or single region).
   b) Monitor SLO panels and operator intervention panel.
   c) Escalate to oncall if p99 > target * 2 or error-rate increases > 2x baseline.
4) Ramp or rollback (decision gates)
   a) If cost-savings or SLO-preservation meet hypothesis -> ramp to 10% then 50% using pre-defined step intervals.
   b) If quality regression > threshold or operator rollbacks > 1 -> rollback immediately, file incident.
5) Post-run analysis (within 48 hours)
   a) Populate experiment report template (see artifacts).
   b) Archive synthetic trace samples and evaluation results.

Rollback quick commands (examples)
--------------------------------
- Immediate global rollback: CLI helper
  - redwoodctl rollout cancel --experiment EXP-001 --force
- Regional undo (eu-west):
  - redwoodctl routing set-region-weight --region eu-west --weight 1.0 --experiment EXP-001
- Re-enable primary model:
  - redwoodctl model set-default --model redwood/llama-70b --variant baseline --experiment EXP-001
Include these command snippets in runbook templates and verify operator RBAC before using.

Decision criteria matrix (accept/ramp/abandon)
--------------------------------------------
- Accept: p95 latency maintained within 10% of baseline AND eval regression <= 3% AND hourly cost delta within budgeted threshold.
- Ramp: p95 within 20% and eval regression <= 7% with operator acceptance.
- Abandon: p95 > 20% degradation OR eval regression > 10% OR unexpected customer errors in the error-tracking system.
Document reasons in experiment report.

Artifacts to capture and store
----------------------------
- Experiment report (.md) with: hypothesis, traffic profile, duration, metrics before/after, cost calculations, operator notes.
- Trace bundle (link to S3) and synthetic eval outputs (json).
- Dashboard snapshot and Prometheus queries used.
- Postmortem if rollback occurred.

Operational responsibilities and ownership
----------------------------------------
- Owner: platform-ops (primary contact: oncall@platform) for run coordination.
- Instrumentation: runtime-team for trace and metric changes.
- Cost modeling: finance-eng liaison for hourly cost validation.
- Security review: security-team if any customer data is used in synthetic prompts.

Safety and customer communication
--------------------------------
- For tenant-facing throttles or degradations that materially impact customer SLAs, coordinate with Customer Success for banner messaging and QBR notes.
- For enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private deployments, require explicit sign-off per the customer SLAs before ramping.

Retrospective template (post-experiment)
--------------------------------------
1) Summary: one-paragraph outcome
2) Metrics: baseline vs. experiment (latency, error-rate, cost, eval pass-rate)
3) What went well
4) What failed / surprises
5) Action items (owner + due date)
6) Decision: accept/ramp/abandon

Appendices
----------
A. Sample PromQL snippets
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",experiment_id=~"EXP-.*"}[5m])) by (le, region))
- fallback rate: sum(rate(fallback_reason_total[1m])) by (fallback_variant)

B. Template experiment report checklist (copy into new experiment ticket)
- Experiment ID: 
- Owner: 
- Hypothesis: 
- Synthetic promptset id: 
- Baseline run links: 
- Dashboard link: 
- Rollback commands verified: Y/N
- Customer communication required: Y/N
